newsitem.title: USA: Moody's may improve outlook for D.C.-firm official.
newsitem.headline: Moody's may improve outlook for D.C.-firm official.

text.p: A Moody's Investors Service official said Friday that the outlook for the District of Columbia's bond rating could improve from stable to positive soon as a result of Congress' new D.C. revitalization plan.
"We might be able to reach a conclusion about a change in outlook in the next few weeks," Steven Hochman, senior vice president at Moody's said in a telephone interview.
"(The measure) does have potential for significantly easing parts of the District's fiscal burden," Hochman added.
"It's not that we could change the rating, but the outlook could be brighter," Hochman said.

Hochman was responding to Congress' approval Thursday of a multi-billion-dollar financial and management package for the District. President Clinton, who engineered key sections of the bill, is expected to sign it shortly.
The District currently has a below investment grade rating from major rating agencies, including Moody's. Moody's also has given the city a "stable" outlook.

Hochman said Moody's has one "concern" about the new D.C. plan, which transfers considerable authority over the city's most important agencies from Mayor Marion Barry to D.C.'s two-year-old control board.
"Elected officials appear to be shunted off to the side," Hochman said.
Under the plan, the board would hire an emergency team of consultants to quickly recommend changes in contracting, personnel management and other top functions.

That concerns Moody's because elected officials probably will return to power in the city in several years. "Therefore, they need to be involved in efforts to reform the management and financial aspects of the city," Hochman said.
